research_question: Does the tapered quantile estimator attain the uniform error decay and bootstrap interval coverage predicted by the Phase 3 theory under two preliminary simulation settings?
scope: Preliminary simulation study with two data-generating processes, sample sizes 200 and 1000, and the single baseline of untapered quantile regression.
scope_justification: The two settings isolate the taper boundary effect that the theory identifies as decisive; passing them is necessary for the theory claims to be empirically plausible, which is the bar for preliminary scope.

claim_tests.hypothesis: Maximum absolute coefficient error decreases as sample size grows from 200 to 1000 in both settings.
claim_tests.design: Monte Carlo simulation with 500 replicates per setting and sample size, comparing error distributions across sizes.
claim_tests.falsification_rule: The test is falsified if the median maximum error at size 1000 is not strictly below the median at size 200 in either setting.

claim_tests.hypothesis: Paired bootstrap intervals attain empirical coverage between 93 and 97 percent at interior quantiles.
claim_tests.design: For each independent generated dataset, 500 illustrative paired bootstrap resamples form its coefficient interval. Outer datasets estimate coverage with explicit returned and attempted denominators; the inner resamples are not independent simulation datasets. No fixed bootstrap count is a general contract requirement.
claim_tests.falsification_rule: The test is falsified if coverage falls outside 90 to 99 percent in either setting at size 1000.

estimand.name: maximum absolute coefficient error
estimand.mathematical_definition: The supremum over the quantile grid of the absolute difference between the estimated and true coefficient vectors, in Euclidean norm per coordinate.
estimand.target_population_or_distribution: The sampling distribution induced by each of the two prespecified data-generating processes.
estimand.aggregation: median and upper quartile across the 500 replicates per condition
conditions: interior quantile grid of 19 equally spaced indices
errors drawn from the setting-specific sub-Gaussian law

data_or_simulation_unit.unit_definition: One dataset of n iid observations with a scalar covariate and a continuous outcome generated under the setting-specific design.
data_or_simulation_unit.sampling_or_generation_process: Setting S1 uses Gaussian errors and a linear quantile structure; setting S2 uses Student-t errors with five degrees of freedom and the same linear location, preserving independently defined coefficient truth.
data_or_simulation_unit.independence_structure: All observations are independent within and across replicates.
data_or_simulation_unit.splits: No sample splitting; the estimator and bootstrap use the full dataset.
data_or_simulation_unit.preprocessing: Covariates are centered and scaled to unit variance before estimation.

baselines.name: untapered quantile regression
baselines.rationale: It is the natural ablation: identical objective without the taper sequence, isolating the contribution of the taper.
baselines.implementation_identity: reference quantile regression solver, pinned version tag qrref-2.4.1
baselines.tuning_policy: No tuning parameters; the solver runs at default settings.
baselines.compute_budget: Same per-replicate compute envelope as the candidate method.

verification_checks: unit test reproduces the untapered solution when taper weights are set to one
deterministic seed check reproduces one full replicate bitwise
implementation_strategy.route_rationale: The frozen tapered objective requires custom model code; this is the first project implementation, not reuse of prior verified project code.

tuning_budget.selection_data: A disjoint pilot simulation of 50 replicates, never used for the confirmatory tests.
tuning_budget.search_space: Taper decay exponent in the set {1.5, 2.0, 2.5}; all other parameters fixed by the method definition.
tuning_budget.optimization_rule: Select the exponent minimizing pilot median maximum error.
tuning_budget.compute_limit: 200 core-hours total for pilot and confirmatory runs.
tuning_budget.fairness_rule: The baseline receives the same replicate count and compute envelope as the candidate.

metrics.name: maximum absolute coefficient error
metrics.definition: Supremum of per-coordinate absolute estimation error over the quantile grid.

metrics.name: bootstrap interval coverage
metrics.definition: Coverage among returned intervals: number of returned nominal 95 percent coefficient intervals containing the independently known coefficient, divided by returned intervals. Also report interval-return among attempted full procedures and joint return-and-cover among attempted procedures; administratively unrun datasets stay separate.
metrics.uncertainty_method: Wilson score interval for the coverage proportion

repetitions_and_uncertainty.random_seed_policy: Seeds are drawn from a master seed of 20260816 by a counter-based generator recorded per replicate.
repetitions_and_uncertainty.interval_or_error_method: Outer repetitions are independent generated datasets. A paired bootstrap within each dataset forms intervals for the declared coefficient target; its inner resamples do not increase the independent-dataset count. Summarize error across outer datasets with the declared median bootstrap interval; report interval-return, coverage among returns, and joint return-and-cover separately, using Wilson intervals with explicit attempted/returned denominators.
repetitions_and_uncertainty.target_precision: Illustrative allocation of 500 outer datasets per declared setting/size; this is not a universal quota or an achieved precision claim. Report actual Monte Carlo uncertainty and completed, failed and unrun counts.

multiplicity.family_definition: The two claim tests form one confirmatory family.
multiplicity.correction_method: Holm step-down correction across the two tests.
multiplicity.decision_rule: A claim is supported only if its test passes at the Holm-adjusted 0.05 level.

stopping_rules.condition: The cumulative compute usage reaches the 200 core-hour limit before all replicates finish.
stopping_rules.action: Stop launching new replicates and report results with the achieved replicate count flagged as a deviation.

leakage_checks.risk: Tuning on confirmatory data would inflate apparent performance.
leakage_checks.procedure: Verify by seed audit that no confirmatory replicate seed appears in the pilot seed list.
leakage_checks.failure_action: Discard the tuning choice, refit with the default exponent 2.0, and record a deviation.

decision_thresholds.criterion: Median maximum error at size 1000 is at least 30 percent below the median at size 200 in both settings.
decision_thresholds.interpretation: Passing supports the uniform consistency claim at preliminary scope; failing blocks progression to comprehensive evaluation.

decision_thresholds.criterion: Coverage lies within 93 to 97 percent at interior quantiles at size 1000 in both settings.
decision_thresholds.interpretation: Passing supports the bootstrap validity claim; coverage below 93 percent contradicts it at preliminary scope.

data_sources.label: Deterministic reference inputs
data_sources.description_markdown: Planned deterministic reference check; this structural example does not retain or claim a completed reference solver. The retained README makes that limitation explicit.
data_sources.mapping_markdown: Declared covariate/outcome arrays and coefficients use the same standardized units as the selected method.

data_sources.label: Independent S1/S2 simulation mechanisms
data_sources.description_markdown: Illustrative S1: $X_i\sim N(0,1)$, $Y_i=1+X_i+\epsilon_i$, with independent $\epsilon_i\sim N(0,1)$, so $Q_{Y|X}(\tau|x)=1+x+\Phi^{-1}(\tau)$. S2 uses independent $t_5$ errors and location $1+x$. The retained source computes population quantiles independently of any fitted estimator. Independent seeds generate independent datasets; neither bootstrap draws nor internal solver fits increase that count.
data_sources.mapping_markdown: x is a unitless covariate and y is an outcome in declared outcome units. Preserve the centering/scaling transformation in target comparisons; no researcher-supplied actual dataset is represented.
